chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Husayn ibn Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man feels that there is moisture on his garment while he is praying, he should take his penis with the edge of his garment and wipe it on his thigh. If it is moisture that he recognizes, he should perform ablution and repeat the prayer; and if it is not moisture, then that is from Satan.
ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if he feels moisture on his clothes during prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in ritual purity, distinguishing between certain doubt (*shakk al-mutma'in*) and minor doubt (*shakk al-mubham*). By attributing unrecognized moisture to Satan, it encourages believers to maintain spiritual confidence and avoid excessive scrupulosity (*waswas*) during worship, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence.
